arcade_owner.phase_source: The ordinary ROM renderer waits for VBlank at $1FC7, increments $6059, then increments shared $605A whenever the new $6059 low three bits are zero. Eligible player and ordinary roaming records use [$605A & 3]; the base families in $0C8B remain below $D8 and have attribute bit 4 clear. This is one shared ordinary pose clock, separate from movement dispatch.
arcade_owner.den_release_correction: A10's corrected callback-indexed raw RAM and exact pixels show the visible waiting actor handed from $602B to $6030; status $81 is renderer-visible but movement-ineligible. It uses ordinary Part-1 art and $605A. No independent den pose-clock family is established.
arcade_owner.scope_exclusions: The $596D startup script bypasses the ordinary actor phase; A10 identifies its only direct caller as a $9002 bit-6-gated Free Play startup path and excludes it from normal gameplay acceptance. Death art remains a separately measured special sequence.

coco_owner.player: PLAYER_ANIM_TIMER ($50) and PLAYER_ANIM ($4F) form a 4-state phase. player_animation_tick decrements the timer and reloads 8 on expiry, then advances phase modulo 4. In the normal adaptive gameplay binding it runs once per scheduled gameplay tick before player movement dispatch. It is suppressed during pickup and most death states; initial entry and death handling are separate states.
coco_owner.enemy: ENEMY_TIMER ($55) and ENEMY_ANIM ($54) reset to 8 and phase 0. enemy_tick_impl decrements once per normal tick and advances ENEMY_ANIM modulo 4 at expiry. Freeze gates movement but not this pose timer. enemy_release_impl does not reset the shared phase.
coco_owner.roaming_and_dormant: Both roaming drawing and dormant nest cache drawing select through enemy_frame_number/draw_enemy_stage and ENEMY_ANIM. The cache builder temporarily iterates phases 0-3, then restores the live phase. Static source shows one CoCo enemy pose owner across roaming and den; no separate den clock is present.
coco_owner.logical_cadence_result: The ordinary CoCo source period is 8 scheduled ticks for both sampled player and enemy clocks, matching the arcade renderer's one phase increment per 8 VBlank waits. The existing B10 player trace maps all 16 logical phase-origin transitions to 8 ticks and does not justify lengthening a timer. No enemy pixel cadence or defect is inferred from the player-only B10 result.
coco_owner.phase_origin_limit: The CoCo stores PLAYER_ANIM and ENEMY_ANIM independently, while arcade ordinary actors share $605A. Timer periods match, but exact current enemy publication and relative pose origin are not established by this source audit; this is the remaining ordinary comparison gate, not a confirmed defect.

enemy.coverage_implication: Eight art families share the same frame-index phase and generated rotation rule; no 8-family by 4-direction timing matrix is justified without evidence of an independent clock or family-specific mismatch. Part-1's first family has existing exact arcade source poses 11,10,9,10.

BUG-011's original scope is Done; later BUG-050 owns the current uniform 32-Vbord instruction colour cycle and is Done, while BUG-048 owns current complete-ROM presentation palette/HUD work and is Done. These profile-specific presentation clocks are outside BUG-080 ordinary gameplay acceptance; Done status is not evidence that every current ROM profile has identical timing.

BUG-010's attract actor fidelity scope is Done. This mode is outside BUG-080 ordinary gameplay acceptance; any new current-profile attract timing discrepancy needs its own discriminating evidence.
separate_presentation_modes.death_and_pickup: Dedicated sequence/suppression paths remain excluded by the Draft's ordinary dwell scope unless an independently measured conflicting gameplay result appears.
